uncited: Unlike [Leaf Node Representation](3000-leaf-node-representation.md), which defines the internal structure of a leaf, this method computes the external indexing required to map leaf nodes to a flat memory space.
**Inputs:** An OpenVDB tree (`m_domainGrid->tree()`).
**Outputs:** A vector `m_leafOffsets` containing cumulative offsets, and an integer `m_totalVoxels`.
Create a `LeafManager` instance wrapping the tree to facilitate leaf counting.
Resize `m_leafOffsets` to hold $N+1$ elements.
Calculate `m_totalVoxels` as $N \times \text{LeafNodeType::SIZE}$.
Generate a sequence of indices from $0$ to $N-1$.
Compute offsets in parallel: for each index $i$, set `m_leafOffsets[i] = i * LeafNodeType::SIZE`.
Set the final offset `m_leafOffsets[N]` to `m_totalVoxels`.
This final element acts as a boundary marker for parallel iteration ranges.
Not given in the sources for other configurations.
- If `num_leaves` is 0, the vector contains two zeros.
- **Time Complexity:** $O(N)$, where $N$ is the number of leaves.
The parallel transform scales with available cores.
- **Memory Complexity:** $O(N)$ for the offset vector.
Provides a clean boundary marker for subsequent parallel loops.
Does not handle variable-sized leaves or sparse leaf distributions differently than dense ones (it counts active leaves).
- **When to use:** When preparing for bulk data transfer into OpenVDB leaf nodes.
- **When not to use:** If leaf sizes vary or if a different memory layout is required.
It is part of the index building pipeline for efficient volume rendering on GPU/CPU hybrid architectures.
